transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-08-05
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Amy Chen (MetroCare CTO), Rajesh Kumar (Platform Lead), Lena Ortiz (Security), Tom Ellis (Eng)

Summary: Quick product walkthrough focused on rate limiting, quotas, and multi-tenant controls (org/project keys) for MetroCare's planned pilot. Discussed hosted vs dedicated controls, per-project quotas, SSO/RBAC requirements, audit logs, and next steps for a 4-week pilot.

00:00 Jordan: hey team, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Sofia our solutions engineer, quick run through agenda — show the console, org vs project keys, demo per-project rate limits, then security questions and next steps
00:18 Amy: thanks Jordan, quick context — we're evaluating vendors for inference serving, main pain is multi-tenant isolation and cost controls; we run multiple product teams in same account and need per-team quotas
00:35 Sofia: got it, we'll show both API and Console flows; note, some product names might be slightly off in the transcript, but you'll see the flow
01:02 Sofia: first slide — orgs, projects, keys. org is the top level for MetroCare, projects map to individual product teams. org-level keys provide global admin, project keys scoped with quotas and can be rotated or revoked independently
01:25 Rajesh: can project keys be pinned to specific model families or regions?
01:34 Sofia: yes, you can restrict by model tags and region routing. for example, production project can be limited to 'redwood-gpt-large-quant' in us-west while dev projects can only hit cheaper endpoints
01:58 Jordan: showing the Console now — Dashboard -> Billing & Quotas -> Project Limits. you'll see per-project QPS, token quotas (monthly), and burst windows
02:20 [screen share noise] Sofia: i'll create a new project 'mc-sales' and show attaching a project key — creating key... there we go, copy/paste redacted in the HUD
02:48 Tom: when you say burst window, how does that affect billing? is burst overage billed?
03:01 Jordan: default is to allow burst within a configured window and meter it. we show both consumed tokens and projected cost, and you get alerts when you hit thresholds. overages can either be blocked or allowed (with billing) depending on policy
03:28 Lena: we need strict blocking for PHI-related routes, can you set different policies per project?
03:40 Sofia: absolutely — you can set rule sets per project; for PHI projects we recommend blocking on overage and also forcing route to dedicated/private infra. it's a per-project policy
04:10 Rajesh: how do we map our internal RBAC to Redwood projects? we use Okta SAML and groups
04:22 Jordan: we support SAML SSO, SCIM for groups. you can map Okta groups to Redwood roles, then scope access to projects. Sofia, maybe show the IAM screen
04:35 Sofia: yeah — Identity -> SSO -> Group mappings. you can tie a group to project-admin or project-developer. audit logs are retained (configurable). note we keep logs in encrypted storage and they can be exported to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export
05:05 Amy: retention length, we have a 7 year audit requirement for some records, is that possible?
05:12 Sofia: seven years is longer than our default, but we do offer extended retention as an add-on or via customer-managed S3 with our Private deployment. we'll flag this for the security deep dive
05:30 [15s pause while screen redraws]
05:46 Jordan: moving to rate limiting patterns — global vs per-org vs per-project. default is per-project quotas; you can also set an org-wide soft cap that applies across projects to control overall spend
06:15 Sofia: demo: set project mc-sales token quota to 10M/month, set QPS limit to 25, burst to 100 for 30s window. trying a quick generation to show throttling behavior
06:42 Sofia: making an API call... 200 OK, tokens consumed 47, no throttle. now I'll spike concurrent requests to hit limit
07:02 [audio overlap] Sofia: ok hitting rate limit... 429 responses start at 07:06. see console, requests show as 'throttled', with reason code 'project_quota_exceeded' (this is our internal code)
07:28 Tom: when throttle happens does the client SDK auto-retry?
07:36 Jordan: SDK has configurable backoff; by default we give exponential backoff and a Retry-After header. you can choose to queue on client side or return error immediately for logic in your app
07:50 Rajesh: and is there per-route limits? the health app wants to limit embedding calls differently than chat calls
08:05 Sofia: yes, you can set route-level policies in the Console: embeddings vs generation vs chat each can have separate QPS and token quotas
08:27 Amy: curious about org vs project keys lifecycle — if I rotate an org key, do project keys remain valid?
08:38 Sofia: project keys are independent; rotating org admin keys doesn't invalidate project keys. you can revoke keys at any time; we also support key expiry for auto-rotation
09:00 Lena: auditability — we need proofs for key rotation and who did it
09:08 Jordan: all key ops are logged with actor identity; for SAML users it's the mapped Okta username. logs include request id, actor, timestamp, and old/new key fingerprints
09:28 [small crosstalk] Speaker 1: apologies, audio cut — can you repeat the key mapping bit?
09:40 Sofia: sure — mapping is via SCIM groups. we support role-based permissions and per-project admin roles; I'll share the mapping doc after the call
10:05 Jordan: switching to pricing + quotas interplay — you can set soft quotas to alert and hard quotas to block. for pilot we suggest soft quotas first and then enforce hard quotas when you go live
10:28 Tom: for pilot we also want spend alarms pushed to our Slack and to a PagerDuty escalation
10:36 Sofia: we have webhooks for alerts and Cloud integrations; we'll add a sample PagerDuty webhook and a Slack integration snippet in the notes
10:57 Rajesh: performance question — if we route a PHI project to dedicated GPUs, does that change how quotas/billing are computed?
11:08 Jordan: yes, dedicated capacity is priced differently; quotas are still enforced but billing is tied to reserved capacity plus per-token adjustments for overages. Sofia: can you show a dedicated pool config?
11:25 Sofia: here — Dedicated -> Pools -> Create. you can pin projects to a pool and define reserved throughput. the pool exposes its own quota meter and can be configured with SLOs and fallback policies
11:48 Amy: fallback — if dedicated pool is full, can requests fall back to hosted? that's not acceptable for PHI
11:58 Sofia: correct, we recommend no-fallback for PHI projects. you can set fail-open for non-PHI dev projects but fail-closed for regulated data, and also route only within VPC for private deployments
12:20 [note about shared doc: link to deck: https://redwood-demo/metrocare/rate-limits-deck ]
12:35 Jordan: quick demo of API usage for project keys — header Authorization: Bearer <PROJECT_KEY>. I'll make a call showing token usage reflected in Project Quotas stream
12:50 Sofia: also note rate limiting headers we return: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After. SDK surfaces these as well
13:05 Rajesh: do we support per-customer metering export for chargebacks? we need to bill internal teams monthly
13:18 Jordan: yes, cost attribution per project is in the billing export CSV and via the API; you can fetch per-project usage daily and integrate into your internal billing tables
13:40 Lena: security review next steps — we want SOC2 documentation, pen test results, and data flow diagrams
13:50 Jordan: we'll attach SOC2 and recent pentest summary. Sofia will set up a security deep dive to go over KMS/HSM options and audit retention
14:10 [Sofia types, link pasted in chat] Sofia: adding link to org-project-keys doc and sample ACL policy (https://redwood-demo/metrocare/org-project-keys.md)
14:25 Tom: can we demo a break-glass scenario where an ops user needs emergency access across projects?
14:35 Sofia: yes — break-glass is an org-level temporary role. we can create time-limited tokens and they are marked in audit logs; they also require justification and an approver if you enable that flow
14:55 Amy: timeline — we want to pilot next month, 4 weeks, limited to 3 projects: patient-messaging, billing-ml, internal-search. goals: validate per-project quotas, cost attribution, and SSO mapping
15:10 Jordan: sounds good. recommended pilot steps: 1) hands-on setup + sample policies, 2) run benchmarking for typical payloads (Sofia will run), 3) security sign-off, 4) formal kickoff
15:28 Sofia: for benchmarking I'll need sample payload sizes and expected seq lengths; Rajesh can share a toy dataset or traffic profile
15:40 Rajesh: will send traffic profile and example prompt shapes by 2025-08-07
15:50 Jordan: any objections or gotchas we didn't cover?
16:02 Amy: just one — we need per-route blocking for PII endpoints, you mentioned route-level policies, good
16:12 Lena: also want to confirm retention export to our S3 with customer-managed encryption
16:20 Sofia: that's supported in Private or via export for Hosted with CMAK integration, we'll detail both options in the security notes
16:35 Jordan: wrap-up recap: we'll send the recording, slides, org-project-keys doc, and pricing. action items: Jordan send pricing + doc, Sofia schedule security deep dive, Sofia prepare pilot config and ACL samples, Rajesh send traffic profile, Amy confirm pilot stakeholders
16:55 Amy: thanks, recording would be great. can you also include the sample PagerDuty webhook config?
17:05 Jordan: yes, will include. thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email
17:12 [call ends] 

Notes about transcript quality: some words auto-transcribed (e.g., 'KV cache' as 'K V cache'), occasional speaker labels replaced with 'Speaker 1'. Links and doc names are representative and point to internal Redwood demo locations.

References shared during the call: https://redwood-demo/metrocare/rate-limits-deck , https://redwood-demo/metrocare/org-project-keys.md , pricing sheet (shared privately)

End of transcript.
